Even with the Texans coming out of their bye week, Montgomery still isn't ready to return to the lineup. Additionally, Jawhar Jordan (quad) is also still out for Houston. With both backs sidelined in Week 7 against the Giants, Marks handled all 19 running-back carries for the Texans. The volume alone puts Marks in the RB1/2 conversation for fantasy this week.
The veteran linebacker appears ready to go for Sunday's game against the winless Chargers. Al-Shaair has recorded 58 tackles (22 solo) and a pair of pass breakups across six starts this season.

away.injury_description: Despite the Colts' 2-6 start to the season, Taylor has remained the engine that drives the offense, racking up 169 touches for 812 yards from scrimmage and eight rushing TDs. The seventh-year pro thus sits 188 total yards shy of reaching 1,000 such yards for the sixth time in his career, so if the right offer crosses Indianapolis' desk, he'd be a vast upgrade for most backfields in the NFL.

Haulcy appeared on Friday's injury report with an ankle injury. The strong safety initially entered the weekend listed as questionable but has now been downgraded to out ahead of Sunday's contest. Second-year safety Hunter Wohler is set to start at safety alongside Cam Bynum against the Cowboys.

Coming off a torn right Achilles last Dec. 7, Jones has struggled for much of the season but especially over the last five contests, a stretch that has included 186.2 passing yards per game, 5.5 YPA and a 2:6 TD:INT. After the last two games in particular, head coach Shane Steichen first decided to stick with Jones as the starter in Week 8 at Jacksonville, and after benching him for Anthony Richardson in that matchup, he eventually opted to stay with Jones for Week 9 action. Despite the uneven play, Baltimore reportedly checked in with Indianapolis before trading for Jacoby Brissett, and Rapoport and Schefter speculated the Vikings are a team that may have interest in Jones, who spent the final month-plus of the 2024 campaign with the organization.

Walley hurt his knee in Week 7 against Minnesota and wasn't able to play last Sunday versus the Jaguars. He's still bothered by the issue and is set to miss a second straight game. Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris again figure to log more defensive snaps as a result.

Gould missed Indianapolis' previous two games while in concussion protocol. However, he was a full practice participant throughout this week and has been cleared to suit up by an independent neurologist. Gould likely will return to his usual specialist role as a kickoff and punt returner, though he probably won't be involved much in the passing game given that he's logged just one offensive snap through six games this season.

Washington's elevation is his second of the campaign. He was active for Week 5 and logged nine offensive snaps, along with three special-teams snaps, against Cincinnati, but he finished without any touches or targets. His workload against the Lions will likely depend on whether Jaylen Wright and Kaytron Allen, both of whom are questionable due to quad injuries, are able to suit up.

Gonzalez has worked as Miami's gameday kicker each of the past two weeks and will do so again versus Detroit on Sunday. He's performed adequately so far, going 2-for-3 on field-goal tries and 5-for-5 on extra-point attempts. This is Gonzalez's third and final elevation, so the Dolphins would need to sign him to the active roster to continue having him kick in games beyond this weekend.

Proctor suffered a concussion in Week 7 against the Jets and didn't play this past Sunday versus New England. However, he was a full participant in all three of Miami's practices this week and has cleared concussion protocol. Proctor is therefore set to reclaim his starting role at left guard.

Muhammad missed last week's victory over the Seahawks due to a toe injury sustained in Week 7, but it appears he will miss only the lone contest.

Monangai was able to get back on the practice field Friday for the first time since suffering a turf-toe injury versus the Jets on Oct. 4, but his limited showing in that session seemingly won't be enough to clear him to suit up Sunday. The Bears have a Week 10 bye on tap, so it comes as no surprise that the team likely will hold off on Monangai's return for two more weeks. Yet again, D'Andre Swift will pace Chicago's backfield this weekend, with Roschon Johnson also on hand for RB reps.

Ahmed is set to be elevated for the first time since signing with Chicago's practice squad in September. With Zavier Scott (wrist) being placed on injured reserve Thursday and Kyle Monangai dealing with thumb and toe injuries, Ahmed could be called upon to provide additional depth behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson against Tampa Bay.

After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.

away.injury_description: Banks landed on IR in late September and was initially expected to be sidelined at least 10 weeks. If he does play, Banks will likely slide back into the starting left tackle role ahead of Asim Richards (ankle), who is also questionable.

White has been on New Orleans' practice squad all season, waiting for a gameday opportunity. He'll get that chance Sunday after Kendre Miller was waived Saturday and CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) was ruled out from facing the Browns. With that said, White may not get an extensive look, as Alvin Kamara and possibly Audric Estime are ahead of him on the RB depth chart.

Smyth is set to take over as New Orleans' kicker beginning with Sunday's matchup against Cleveland, so the elevation was a necessary move. He'll be replacing Daniel Carlson, who was released Tuesday. The Browns have had 19 field-goal tries against them this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL, so Smyth could be busy in his 2026 debut.

Tyson thus is one step closer to making his NFL debut after missing the first eight weeks of the campaign due to hamstring issues that have bothered him since the start of training camp. With a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff on tap Sunday, his status will be clarified, one way or another, about 90 minutes before that point.

Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

Mays sustained a low-ankle sprain in the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. The center was unable to participate in Week 9 prep while dealing with the issue and will not be able to suit up for Sunday's game. Juice Scruggs is set to start at center while Mays is sidelined.
Wonnum was unable to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's contest. The defensive end did not practice at all during Week 9 prep and remains sidelined with the head injury.

The upgrade to limited participation was enough to clear Wirfs of any injury designation, and the veteran protector is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest.

Smith was limited at practice by an ankle issue Wednesday and Thursday, but he managed to practice in full Friday and will avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend. He projects to start at safety next to Antoine Winfield in Week 9.

Trotter was limited by an illness at practice ahead of Week 8, and he ultimately secured a season-low six stops in the win. The rookie linebacker has put together quite the impressive start to his first NFL campaign, compiling 68 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pick-six over seven contests so far.

Parrish was able to notch multiple passes defensed for the fifth straight game, and he was able to reel in his second interception of the year, jumping in front of a short pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix in the second quarter. Remigio has dealt with a hip issue this week but was able to log full practice sessions Thursday and Friday. That likely means he's trending toward playing Sunday, though his availability isn't a certainty. Remigio has a key role in the return game for Kansas City but has played just two offensive snaps through seven games.

Reid added that the rookie Delane is "making progress" but isn't quite ready to make his return, marking the second straight game the 22-year-old will miss. Delane has 27 tackles (17 solo), five pass deflections and one interception in five games this season.

Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.

Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.

away.injury_description: Adams was placed on IR in early October and missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and was limited in all three of Arizona's practices this week. Now that he's been activated, Adams is eligible to suit up Sunday, and if he returns he'll likely reclaim his starting role at right guard.

Bowman was previously elevated for Week 6, when he logged four snaps on special teams (and none on offense) against the Rams. His usage could be similarly limited Sunday against Seattle, as the Cardinals have three healthy tight ends (Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano) ahead of Bowman in the pecking order.

Ford signed with Arizona's practice squad Oct. 14 and is now set to potentially make his gameday debut with the team Sunday in Seattle. He spent his first four NFL campaigns with Cleveland and averaged an acceptable 4.3 yards per carry with seven rushing touchdowns over 340 totes while also accumulating 647 yards and an additional five touchdowns on 107 catches across 57 games. Given that level of experience, it will be interesting to see how much the Cardinals utilize Ford on Sunday, though Tyler Allgeier is slated to work as the team's lead back, and Evan Hull will also factor into the mix.

Gaines continues to battle a knee injury and will miss his third straight game. Hayden Conner may make another start at right guard, though Isaiah Adams (ankle) -- who has been deemed questionable -- could take on that role if he's activated from IR on Saturday.

Williams made an early exit from Sunday's loss to Dallas after hurting his knee. He didn't practice at all this week and is set to miss the first game of his career. The rookie has started four of Arizona's first eight contests of the campaign.

Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to suit up Sunday, so Mafah could work as the Giants' No. 3 RB behind Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.

He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.

A lingering groin issue held Thomas to limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday to avoid a designation heading into the weekend. The star left tackle will therefore continue to anchor the offensive line for the first place Giants.

He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.

Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.

Boerkircher was tied with Parker Washington for the second-most receiving yards on the team with 61. This game marks the fourth time this season that the rookie has surpassed 30 snaps on offense. Boerkircher has made a name for himself as Jacksonville's No. 2 option at tight end behind Brenton Strange.

This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.

away.injury_description: Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a turf-toe injury. Brissett's experience gives the team a chance to get back to winning ways after losing four games in a row.

Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.

Smith led his team in tackles on a night when Baltimore had a hard time slowing down the Jaguars' offense. Though he's been bothered by knee and foot issues in recent weeks, the veteran linebacker logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Thursday. Smith is well on his way to another triple-digit tackle campaign with 74 stops, including 2.0 sacks, along with an interception and two forced fumbles through nine contests.

With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

He logged just two offensive snaps and didn't get a touch or target in that game, but he he did rack up 50 yards on two kick returns. Schrader figures to fill a similar role against the Panthers as the No. 3 RB behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.
